title: Jack Schlossberg disappears amid humiliating personal crisis
text:
By EMILY CRANE

Published:  09:15 AEST, 15 September 2026   |  Updated:  22:13 AEST, 15 September 2026

731

View  comments

Kennedy heir Jack Schlossberg was a constant man about town as he tried to drum up votes and rake in donations at the height of his New York congressional campaign.

But just months on from his humiliating defeat, the 33-year-old political nepo baby  mysteriously vanished altogether, with his tight-knit family apparently whisking him away to prevent a potential spiral, sources told the Daily Mail.

President John F Kennedy's only grandson appears to have ditched his usual routine and has be MIA from his Chelsea apartment building of late, according to the sources.

'People haven't seen him,' one source inside the building said.

'At one point, food was being delivered and sat outside overnight. That was when people really started wondering where Jack had gone.'

Schlossberg, who failed spectacularly in his bid to get elected to Congress this past June despite being part of one of America's most powerful political families, took the bruising loss much harder than anyone expected, sources said.

So much so that his family - including mom Caroline Kennedy - apparently jumped into action right after election night, according to insiders.

'The family swooped in after the loss and whisked him away,' one source claimed.

Kennedy heir Jack Schlossberg, 33, has mysteriously disappeared of late - with his tight-knit family whisking him away to prevent a potential spiral after his bruising election defeat. He is pictured with his mom, Caroline Kennedy, on the campaign trail in May

Schlossberg, pictured on election night, failed spectacularly in his bid to get elected to Congress this past June - despite being part of one of America's most powerful political families

'They knew how badly he was hurting. The last thing they wanted was Jack sitting alone in that apartment staring at election results.'

Ultimately, Schlossberg finished a distant third in the Democratic primary for New York's 12th congressional district, which covers large swathes of Manhattan's Upper East Side, Upper West Side and Midtown.

The results, which saw him secure just 10.8 percent of the votes, were particularly painful given he couldn't even win over voters in his own Chelsea neighborhood, sources said.

'Jack was 100 percent sure he was going to win,' one insider said. 'The election loss really hurt. He wasn't prepared for this result.'

'His building is an entire city block and he couldn't even win there,' the source added.

'Imagine believing you're about to be elected to Congress and then discovering you couldn't carry your own immediate neighborhood. That was devastating.'

Still, a source close to Schlossberg was quick to dismiss speculation he was holed up somewhere in the wake of the defeat, telling the Daily Mail he has spent part of the summer with his family in Martha's Vineyard.

'While he did spend time in Martha's Vineyard with his family, he's also been back multiple times to the city and had multiple meetings, including next steps and ideas he has for the party ahead of the midterms,' a source familiar with his movements said.

Schlossberg posted a cryptic photo on social media late Tuesday of him sitting in front of a camera with the caption: 'What am I cooking this time ?!'

These days, Schlossberg has been posting videos of himself cooking and volunteering, which is in stark contrast to his campaigning days

Schlossberg was flanked by his mom, Caroline Kennedy, at his election night watch party back in June

'He's even got a meeting scheduled with one of the folks he ran in the 12th primary with. He really wasn't whisked [away].'

'Schlossberg has a lot of options and he's trying to nail down what to do, including TV opportunities with Netflix and Prime Time,' the source added.

'The future is bright.'

Schlossberg, for his part, posted a cryptic photo on social media last Tuesday of him sitting in front of a camera with the caption: 'What am I cooking this time?!'

He has also taken to sharing the odd cooking post and photos of him volunteering - with just rare snippets of political criticism sprinkled in.

It is in stark contrast to when Schlossberg was flooding Instagram with videos and photos of him schmoozing New Yorkers mid-campaign.

The political scion has largely stayed out of the headlines, too, following his defeat - aside from when reports surfaced last week about his friends wanting to set him up with a newly single Rep. Alexandria Ocasio Cortez.

Reacting to the news, Schlossberg cheekily told the New York Post: 'I respect her a lot - she can do way better than me!'

Ahead of election day, 'Jack Schlossberg for Congress' signs were spotted all over his apartment building

Claims that Schlossberg was just a pampered political prince with no real-world experience dogged his campaign

It comes after Schlossberg's campaign was dogged, in part, by reports of high turnover of campaign staff and internal dissatisfaction with the candidate.

Claims that Schlossberg was just a pampered political prince with no real-world experience also added fuel to the fire. Schlossberg's critics argued, in part, that he had done little in his career to warrant a congressional seat.

Before his decision to take a stab at elective politics, Schlossberg was best known for online trolling, including a clip questioning whether Second Lady Usha Vance was 'hotter' than his own grandmother Jacqueline Kennedy and another suggesting JD Vance had killed Pope Francis who died a day after a meeting with the vice president.

He also labeled his cousin Robert F Kennedy Jr as a 'Russian asset.'

There was also a particularly disturbing online rant at Alan Dershowitz, the lawyer and friend of the late Senator Ted Kennedy, during which Schlossberg accused him of killing his wife and being tied to Jeffrey Epstein.

'Schlossberg was a joke from the beginning. The only surprising thing about this election is he got ten percent of voters,' Dershowitz told the Daily Mail in the wake of Schlossberg's defeat.

'Why would anybody possibly vote for him, other than to get to touch a Kennedy. He has no qualifications, never held any office, and if his name were John Smith, he wouldn't get a single vote. It's such an insult to the intellect of voters to have a candidate like this even run. I wouldn't vote for him for dog catcher.

'I love the Kennedys, I have very high regard for the Kennedys. This doesn't help their reputation, but the Kennedys can't be blamed for him. The Kennedys are a great family, and they deserve to be respected, and one black sheep shouldn't hurt the reputation of the family,' he added.

The Daily Mail has reached out to Schlossberg.
